Palihapitiya Backs Jensen Huang’s Leadership Style
In a post on
X

, Palihapitiya shared a New York Times report detailing Huang’s alleged use of humiliation to motivate Nvidia employees, saying the revelations made him more interested in working for the billionaire CEO.
“This makes me want to work for him MORE,” Palihapitiya wrote.
He said he would rather work for someone with “ridiculous expectations, impatience and vision” and accept the difficulties that come with such an environment.
According to Palihapitiya, leaders like Huang weed out employees who cannot withstand intense pressure and push organizations toward extraordinary achievements.
“Guys like this will filter out all the mediocre people that can’t take the heat and won’t take you to greatness,” he wrote.
He added that such an approach could leave behind “a team of killers capable of building the largest, most valuable company in the world.”
